session.late_join: spectate until the next round boundary

trust_assumptions: Clients may request legal commands but never author inventory or outcomes
The service identity layer authenticates a player before match join
topology.host_migration: not applicable because no player hosts the match

authority_validation: action identifier has not already been applied
target is legal in canonical state
action cost and cooldown are valid
vote is legal in the current phase

client_can_request: play a card from own hand
authority_validation: card is in the caller's canonical hand
card is legal in the current turn

simulation.tick_rate_basis: This game resolves discrete commands and does not require a continuous simulation tick.
simulation.prediction: Client may preview legal targets but never applies an outcome as final.
simulation.reconciliation: Server command result replaces pending client preview state by action identifier.
simulation.measurement_plan: Measure command resolution, round-trip, queue depth, and reconnect recovery on the supported browser and region matrix.

replication.model: reliable commands plus canonical state snapshots
replication.interest_management: All public match state reaches members; private hand state reaches only its owner.
replication.hidden_state: The server never sends another player's private hand to a client.

transport.rationale: Broad target-browser support and reliable ordered turn commands fit this discrete simulation.
transport.fallback: HTTPS polling is limited to lobby status; an active match requires the WebSocket session.
transport.backpressure: Each connection has a bounded outbound queue; overflow closes the connection and forces a canonical resnapshot on reconnect.

lifecycle.reconnect: A valid short-lived resume token restores membership and sends one canonical authorized snapshot.
lifecycle.disconnect: The server marks the player absent and applies the product-owned turn timeout policy without transferring authority.
lifecycle.version_policy: Reject incompatible protocol versions before match membership or state mutation.

security.identity: Short-lived signed session token bound to player and match
security.authorization: Check match membership, phase, ownership, and action permission for every message.
validation: validate every message against the protocol schema
reject duplicate or stale action identifiers
calculate movement, combat, inventory, and rewards on the server
security.logging: Log event type, result, reason, player id, match id, and sequence only; never log tokens or private hand contents.

alerts: reconnect failures exceed the product-owned threshold
canonical state checksum mismatch is observed

scenarios: two players submit commands at nearly the same time
a client replays an already applied action identifier
a player disconnects while a reward command is pending
an incompatible client attempts to join
a slow reader fills its outbound queue
acceptance: Out-of-turn and duplicate commands leave canonical state unchanged.
Reconnect sends one authorized canonical snapshot and never duplicates a reward.
Private hand state is absent from every unauthorized client capture.
Queue overflow follows the documented close and resnapshot path.

decisions.decision: Use a dedicated authoritative match server
decisions.reason: The game has private hands, persistent rewards, and reconnect requirements.
decisions.evidence: Authority matrix, hidden-state boundary, and reconnect acceptance criteria

decisions.decision: Use WebSocket rather than a peer channel
decisions.reason: The discrete command model needs broad browser support and one independent authority.
decisions.evidence: Target-platform matrix and transport delivery requirements
